newsitem.title: USA: FTC issues jewelry warning for Valentine's Day. [CORRECTED 21:48 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FTC issues jewelry warning for Valentine's Day. [CORRECTED 21:48 GMT]

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission on Monday urged consumers to take care when buying Valentine's Day jewelry and to verify in writing that gold, pearls and other goods were authentic.

"If jewelry is on your list for Valentine's Day, take the time to get in writing a description of what you're buying, whether they claim it's cultured pearls or genuine diamonds," said Bonnie Jansen, a spokeswoman for the FTC.

The warning coincided with an announcement that Zale Corp, which owns the nation's biggest jewelry retail chain with more than 1,300 outlets, had promised to honestly label imitation pearls. (Corrects that warning was not given at a news conference)
Zale agreed to settle government charges it deceptively advertised that its "Ocean Treasures" line used cultured pearls when in fact it used imitation pearls, the FTC said.

A spokewoman for Zale Corp. at its Irving, Texas, headquarters said the company's stores no longer sold either imitation pearls or the "Ocean Treasures" line. Nonetheless, for the next three years Zale will describe the differences between natural, cultured and imitation pearls in information sheets.
Cultured pearls grow as a result of an irritant placed in the animal's shell by humans, while the far cheaper imitation pearls merely simulate the appearance of a pearl, the FTC said.
Natural pearls, formed entirely without human intervention, are more rare and costly, the FTC said.
Consumers can also check "Beloved...Bejeweled...Be Careful," a guide at the FTC web site, http://www.ftc.gov. The FTC has responsiblity for consumer protection.
